topicName: Azure Monitor, Log Analytics Workspaces, and Kusto Query Language (KQL)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering Azure Monitor, Log Analytics Workspaces, and KQL"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this technical tutorial, we will explore the foundational components of observability in Microsoft Azure. You will learn how to configure Log Analytics Workspaces, ingest telemetry data, and write powerful queries using the Kusto Query Language (KQL)."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding Azure Monitor and Log Analytics"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Azure Monitor is a comprehensive solution for collecting, analyzing, and acting on telemetry from your cloud and on-premises environments. At the heart of Azure Monitor Logs is the Log Analytics Workspace. This is a unique environment for log data that acts as a container storing data with its own access control and data retention settings."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Data Sources: Collects metrics and logs from Azure resources, operating systems, containers, and custom application code."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Retention: Retains data for up to 730 days, allowing for long-term auditing and trend analysis."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Access Control: Provides granular permission models using Azure RBAC to secure sensitive operational logs."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Introduction to Kusto Query Language (KQL)"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Kusto Query Language (KQL) is a read-only request used to process data and return results. The language is easy to read and author, providing high-performance data filtering, aggregation, and visualization capabilities. A KQL query always starts with a table name and uses the pipe character (|) to chain operations together."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"AppTraces
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| summarize EventCount = count() by SeverityLevel
| order by EventCount desc"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Advanced Querying Techniques"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"When diagnosing complex production issues, basic filtering is often not enough. You will need to join multiple tables, parse custom log formats, and evaluate time-series trends. Below is an example of joining request logs with exception logs."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"requests
| join kind=inner exceptions on operation_Id
| project timestamp, name, outerMessage, innermostMessage
| take 50"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Best Practices for Production Environments"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always filter by TimeGenerated first to minimize the volume of data scanned by the query engine."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid using wildcards at the beginning of string searches (e.g., *string) as they cannot utilize index lookups efficiently."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use the summarize operator effectively to aggregate metrics and reduce the output payload size."},{"order":18,"type":"heading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"By combining Azure Monitor, Log Analytics Workspaces, and KQL, engineering teams gain deep visibility into the health and performance of their cloud architecture. Continue practicing KQL queries in your own sandbox environments to build operational excellence."}]
